name: Pendulum-Frost
description: Pendulum-Frost is a small ice world whose eccentric orbit causes dramatic tidal stresses as it swings between perihelion and aphelion. The result is a surface laced with fracture networks that open and close with each orbital cycle, accompanied by geysers of ice and ammonia that erupt in rhythmic pulses.

The thin atmosphere is mostly nitrogen with ammonia traces that freeze and fall as frost during the colder orbital phases. The surface oscillates between a relatively smooth ice plain at aphelion and a shattered, geysering chaos at perihelion, transforming the landscape twice per orbit.

The pendulum-like oscillation between states has created a unique geological record in the ice layers, each orbital cycle depositing a distinct stratum. Core samples reveal millions of these layers, providing a precise orbital clock stretching back to the planet's formation.

Scientific interest in Pendulum-Frost centers on its value as a natural chronometer and tidal dynamics laboratory. The water ice reserves are substantial but extraction is complicated by the surface instability, requiring operations to be timed to the calmer aphelion phase of each orbit.
